title: Math grammar coverage on all 28,956 first-pass spans (V1, V2) and the S5 grammar extensions
question: How much of the first pass does the one math grammar read with each rendition's macro table, before and after Lark edit_terminals (V1) and the tokenizer macro reader (V2), by failure and ambiguity category; which extensions gain spans without turning any ok span failed or ambiguous, and where do the remaining failures sit?
method: code/s5_coverage.py parses every span under any_value in 30 single-threaded worker processes (parsers cached per macro classification; 2 s parse timer; the ambiguity resolver's SymPy conversions bounded at 1 s per reading, 4 s per value) with deterministic failure categories from the exception class, the TeX token at the error and the allowed set. Four baselines (spike grammar / edit_terminals / edit_terminals without the %override lines, x spike / tokenizer reader) are compared span by span. code/s5_extensions.py tries 35 candidate blocks (code/s5grammar/ext/) greedily over all spans: kept when they gain spans and turn no ok span failed or ambiguous and no read span failed (a read span already >= 1.5 s that then times out counts as a timing effect, reported per trial); the kept blocks are assembled into code/s5grammar/extension.lark. The frozen I-R2 mathgrammar is not edited. code/s5_report.py writes parse.tsv and coverage.md.
commands: UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$REPO/build/spike-venv uv run --project . --no-sync python code/s5_coverage.py --variant spike --reader spike (and edited/spike, edited/tokenizer, edited-noovr/tokenizer)
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$REPO/build/spike-venv uv run --project . --no-sync python code/s5_coverage.py --variant extended --reader tokenizer [--printer s5]

inputs.role: grammar variants: edit_terminals, ordered_sets, block trials

outputs.role: the extended extension.lark (I-R2 extension + kept S5 blocks)
per span: key, page, kind, offsets, delimiting status, baseline and extended status, detected kind, category or ambiguity cause, ms
coverage by status and category before and after each extension; the 8 partial spans; timing
per trial: transitions, gains by construct, broken spans, timing-boundary spans
run summaries (the per-span run files are not kept; parse.tsv and canonical.tsv carry them)

results.name: v1_spans_changed
results.note: edit_terminals (with or without the regex %override lines) changes no status, kind, category, note or printed tree: no corpus command extends a literal terminal's name (\leftarrow, \quadrant); earlier figures are not overstated on Siegrist

results.name: v2_spans_changed
results.note: the tokenizer reader adds \P on 22 pages but no effective table changes (same fallback body)

results.name: extension_blocks_kept
results.note: rejected: 08 (R = S \times T ok -> ambiguous; refined as 20), 23 (\P(E, X \in A) ok -> ambiguous; refined as 27), 32 inverse images (8 ok spans broken)

results.name: largest_remaining_named_construct
results.note: measure differentials d\mu(x), K(x, dy), d(\mu \times \nu); then inner products 27, text words 25, \prime 21, multinomials 16; the stop criterion (about 50) is met

results.name: parse_ms_median
results.note: baseline -> extended, uncached parses; p99 382 -> 859 ms

results.name: resolver_unbounded_found
results.note: api._Resolver converts readings to SymPy outside the parse timer; Eq(...) evaluated an integral numerically for more than 11 minutes on the first run; bounded here, a port obligation

conclusion: With the rendition macro tables the I-R2 grammar reads 90.3% of the first pass (80.8% ok); V1 and V2 change nothing on Siegrist. Thirty-two extension blocks (tuples, \mapsto, signatures, conditional and set arguments, styled subscripts, set powers and equations, cases and align environments, prose connectives, among others) raise it to 98.0% read and 87.6% ok with no ok span lost; the remaining 586 failures spread over constructs of at most 38 spans. Coverage is a reported figure (plan §1): 87.6% ok is below the brief's 90% reading, so M11 types and converts fewer spans, while keys are unaffected (D1 §6.2). The port carries extension.lark, edit_terminals with ordered_sets=True, and one deadline over the whole read including the resolver.
